app_note: Yogurt cultures ferment milk sugars and create tangy flavor and texture.
risk_note: Live culture status depends on processing and product labeling.

app_note: Lactobacillus is a broad group of bacteria used in many fermented foods.
risk_note: Probiotic claims require strain-specific evidence.

app_note: Bifidobacterium can appear in cultured dairy and probiotic-style foods.
risk_note: Health claims must be strain-specific and source-backed.

app_note: Streptococcus thermophilus is one of the classic yogurt starter cultures.
risk_note: Do not confuse food-culture species with unrelated pathogens by name alone.

functional_purpose: converts alcohol-derived ferment into vinegar flavor
app_note: Acetobacter-related cultures are associated with vinegar-style fermentation.
risk_note: Culture presence does not guarantee live microbes in final food.

app_note: Koji is a fermentation starter used to develop sweetness umami and aroma in several traditional foods.
risk_note: Species and food-grade culture identity matter.

app_note: Miso adds salty fermented umami flavor and body.
risk_note: Contains soy and may contain grains depending on type.

app_note: Soy sauce is a fermented salty seasoning used for umami and color.
risk_note: Contains soy and often wheat unless specified gluten-free tamari.

app_note: Vinegar gives sharp acidity and can help preserve pickled foods.
risk_note: Acidity and flavor vary by vinegar type.

app_note: Kimchi powder brings fermented vegetable spice notes to dry foods.
risk_note: May contain fish shellfish or wheat ingredients depending on recipe.

app_note: Sauerkraut is cabbage transformed by lactic fermentation.
risk_note: Sodium can be high depending on recipe.

app_note: Sourdough starter contains yeasts and bacteria that create rise and tangy flavor.
risk_note: Not automatically gluten-free unless made from gluten-free grains.

app_note: Rennet helps milk form curds during cheesemaking.
risk_note: Source may be animal microbial or fermentation-derived.

app_note: Lactase is used to reduce lactose in dairy products.
risk_note: Lactose-free does not mean milk-allergen-free.

app_note: Amylase helps convert starches into smaller sugars during food processing.
risk_note: Enzyme usually supports processing rather than remaining as a main ingredient effect.

app_note: Proteases break proteins into smaller pieces and can affect tenderness flavor or dough behavior.
risk_note: Source and use vary widely.

app_note: Lipase can help develop dairy-style flavor notes by acting on fats.
risk_note: Usually used for processing or flavor development.

app_note: Invertase can soften fondant-style candy centers by changing sucrose into simpler sugars.
risk_note: Mostly relevant in confectionery.

app_note: Pectinase helps clarify juices and improve fruit processing.
risk_note: Usually a processing aid rather than a consumer-facing nutrient.

app_note: Transglutaminase can bind proteins and change texture in meat seafood or plant-protein products.
risk_note: Should be explained neutrally as a texture enzyme.
